- RIDA returns for 2015 (only ">= double-digit"), 2017, 2018 and 2019 were not found.

evidence.red_flags:
1) Circular sourcing.
- The Portfolio123 Medallion series (2019 39%, 2020 76%, 2021 48%, 2022 19%) matches the Quartr x Acquired chart bar for bar. The forum list is almost certainly copied from it, and the chart's own origin for 2019, 2021 and 2022 is undisclosed.
- The "2025 ~20%" figure appears both in the forum post and in a FUNanc1al blog that labels it "estimated" while also calling Medallion's returns "shrouded in secrecy".
- Every "Medallion +76% in 2020" report traces back to a single unnamed investor quoted by II (Jan 2021).

2) Regulatory AUM mistaken for real AUM.
- Wikipedia's infobox "$130bn AUM (Apr 2021)" cites P&I (Sep 2019). It is Form ADV gross regulatory AUM (YE2017/18), not net capital.
- Wikipedia also says "Medallion $165bn discretionary incl. leverage". $165.97bn was the FIRM's RAUM at YE2019; II reported Medallion's own figure as $34.8bn.
- Acquired (Mar 2024) says the institutional funds "peaked over $100bn, currently $60-70bn". FT/II put RIEF at about $19.6bn and RIDA at about $3.6bn in 2024, so Acquired likely used gross RAUM.
- 13F values ($64-76bn) are long US equity holdings, not AUM.

3) Conflicting fund returns.
- RIEF 2020: -19.43% (monthly data), -19.4% (II 2024), -19.94% (HSBC via II Feb 2021, which in the same article also says "19.4"; possible digit transposition), -22.62% (through Dec 25 only), -19%/-20% (Bloomberg/FT).
- RIEF Jan 2021: -9.46% (monthly data) vs -5.8% (Providence pension report).
- RIDA 2020: -31% to -33.58%. RIDA 2021: 14.56% (Series A), 15% (Bloomberg) or 17% (FT). RIDA 2024: 15.6% (press) vs 15.22% (Series A).
- These spreads reflect share-class or series differences and partial-period cut-offs.

4) II internal errors.
- Nov 2025 calls RIDA's 2024 its best year "since 2021 inception", but RIDA launched in 2012.
- April 2020 cites a 17-19pp gap between Medallion and the other funds, which is inconsistent with the 24% vs -7 to -9% figures in the same article (a 31-33pp gap).
- Nov 2025 "RIEF just under $20bn" repeats the Nov 2024 wording and may be stale; a hedge-fund database showed $16.2bn around Jan 2026.

5) Medallion fees and gross returns.
- Zuckerman and Cornell give 5%/44%; II (Nov 2025) says 4% / 36-44%.
- Acquired and Scrivner give 2020 gross as 149%, while 5/44 math implies about 141% for 76% net.
- Scrivner's "2022 33% gross" implies about 16% net, vs 18-19% elsewhere.

6) Medallion size.
- Press lore puts it at about $10bn, capped at $10-15bn.
- Form ADV feeder gross assets were $20.5bn (YE2020), $28.2bn (YE2021), $25.4bn (YE2022) and $19.3bn (YE2023). These probably include undistributed current-year profits and possibly retained capital.
- Master Medallion Holdings gross assets rose to $61.2bn (YE2025).
- The YE2018 feeder sum ($11.7bn) is below the ~$14bn Zuckerman's numbers imply, suggesting distributions during the year.
- Treat Zuckerman's "$12bn (2024)" as working capital after distributions, and the ADV figures as an upper-bound check.

7) Entity traps seen in results.
- IAPD lists an unrelated "RENAISSANCE TECHNOLOGIES AI SUPERCOMPUTING HEDGE CAPITAL LTD." (CRD 338503, 802- exempt reporting adviser, W 41st St NYC). It is possibly an impersonator; do not confuse it with CRD 106661.
- Other look-alikes: Renaissance Capital (IPO ETF, N-CSR filings), Renaissance Investments (CIBC Canadian mutual funds), RenaissanceRe and Medallion Financial Corp.
- Intellectia.ai's "Renaissance 2025 return 9.64%" is unattributed and most likely a 13F portfolio calculation.

8) GF Trading LLC (the RIDA master) gross assets fell from $9.4bn (YE2014) to $2.8bn (YE2015), then rose to $18.1bn (YE2016). The 2015 filing also lists the vehicles Badger Holdings L.P. ($2.36bn) and Mosel Equities L.P. ($0.94bn). These are unexplained structural changes.

9) Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, Reuters and Business Insider were blocked for direct fetch. Their figures are taken from II, Hedgeweek, Realtid, The Wealth Advisor or Wikipedia relays and are marked accordingly.

- **RIDGE:** 2020 -31%, 2021 +10%; merged into RIDA on 2023-12-31.

evidence.gaps:
I ran out of the shared WebSearch quota (200 calls per turn) partway through. After that I only fetched known URLs directly, so some press coverage I would normally have searched for is probably missing. Gaps that remain:
(1) Medallion net/gross return not found for 2019, 2021 (full year; only Q1 +9.7%), 2023, 2024, 2025 or 2026 YTD. The only 2022 figure is a blog's '33% gross'. II (Jan 2021) implies 2019 was below 76%.
(2) No RIEF/RIDA/RIDGE annual returns found for 2015-2019, 2022, 2023, full-year 2025 (only YTD Oct: RIEF -7.5%, RIDA -10.3%) or 2026 YTD. RIDA and RIDGE are missing for 2021, and RIDGE is missing for full-year 2020.
(3) The private-fund gross asset values from the March 2025 annual ADV (YE2024) could not be obtained. SEC bulk Schedule D data ends 2024-12-31, and IAPD serves only the current filing. YE2024 Medallion/RIEF/RIDA capital is therefore inferred.
(4) From the 2024 filing onward, feeder-level Medallion NAV is no longer itemised. YE2025 has only the master GAV ($61.2B, levered), so Medallion net capital for 2024-2026 is uncertain (roughly $19-36B).
(5) There is no primary source for net AUM of RIEF/RIDA. I estimated it from master GAV divided by leverage ratios calibrated to II's start-2020 figures (RIEF 1.56x, RIDA 2.12x, RIDGE 1.85x). The ratios drift (RIDA ~1.5x at YE2025), so the estimates carry roughly ±25% error.
(6) Headcount is ADV Item 5A, which is approximate, rounded to 10, excludes clerical workers, and is dated at the annual filing (late March). No average or year-end figure is disclosed. No rating-agency or leveraged-finance coverage exists (Renaissance has no public debt).
(7) 2026 YTD: nothing found for any fund. The latest primary data is the 2026-07-01 ADV amendment, which carries YE2025 values.
Derived P&L exists for: Medallion 2015-2018 and 2020; outside funds 2020, 2021 (RIEF only), 2024 and YTD Oct-2025. All other entity-years need other agents' return data.
evidence.red_flags:
- Regulatory AUM conflict for 12/31/2020. ADV Part 1 says $130.86B (II also quotes $130.86B), but the March-30-2021 Part 2A brochure says $115.91B.
- ADV regulatory AUM includes leverage. The YE2019 figure of $166B compares with net assets of about $75B. Master-fund GAVs are also levered (Medallion master $61.2B at YE2025). Only Medallion feeder GAVs (to YE2023) approximate net capital.
- Medallion size: the '$10B cap' folklore (Zuckerman $9.5-10B; Bloomberg 2017) conflicts with ADV feeder NAV sums. Those were $12.5-15.6B at YE2014-2017 and $20.5B, $28.2B, $25.3B and $19.2B at YE2020-2023. Possible causes are undistributed H2 profits at the YE valuation, fee-free employee RF vehicles, and capital growth after 2020 (II Apr-2021: size raised 10%).
- 13F long-holdings values are being presented as AUM: hedgefundalpha says '$63.9B AUM', and Insider Monkey's sidebar shows $77.4B. hedgefundalpha's 'Q1 2026 return -4.58%' is likely 13F-portfolio based, not a fund return.
- Mislabelled date: privatefunddata labels the $96.38B regulatory AUM 'Mar 25'. It is actually the 12/31/2025 figure, filed 2026-04-01; the March 2025 filing reported $91.96B. SmartAsset mixes $96.4B with 'a little over $100B'.
- Entity confusion: IAPD contains an unrelated exempt-reporting adviser, 'RENAISSANCE TECHNOLOGIES AI SUPERCOMPUTING HEDGE CAPITAL LTD.' (CRD 338503), which may be an impostor. Renaissance Investment Management (Kentucky, ~$2.6B) and Renaissance Capital are also different firms.
- II Nov-2025 says RIDA's 2024 was its best 'since its 2021 inception'. RIDA actually launched in Feb 2012 (II Jan-2021; ADV shows the RIDA feeder from 2013).
- II Nov-2025 repeats the Nov-2024 wording 'just under $20 billion, down from nearly $36 billion' for RIEF, so it is likely stale. The YE2025 RIEF master GAV of $21.8B implies roughly $14-19B net.
- RIEF 2020 has three different figures: -19.4% (II 2024), -20% (II Apr-2021) and -22.62% through Dec 25 (HSBC).
- Scrivner blog's 2020 '149% gross' does not match 76% net under 5%/44% fees, which gives ~141%. The blog also cites '400 employees' against ADV's 300-310.
- Medallion fees changed: 5%/44% through 2020, a 4% management fee from 2021-01-01, and 36-44% performance from 2022. Sources that apply 5%/44% to 2021+ will overstate gross returns. II Nov-2025 correctly gives 4% and 36-44%.
- hedgefundalpha says a 'Renaissance Institutional Futures Fund' was launched in Oct 2023. The 2024 and 2026 ADV brochures list only Medallion, RIEF and RIDA, so this is unsupported.
- The Wikipedia infobox's '$130B AUM' cites a 2019 P&I list with a mismatched date.
evidence.summary:
The best primary source here is Renaissance's own SEC filings (CRD 106661). I pulled SEC monthly adviser files, the SEC Form ADV bulk Schedule D private-fund tables, Part 2A brochures from 2020, 2021, Aug-2022, 2024 and 2026, and the current IAPD ADV (2026-07-01).

**Headcount (ADV Item 5A, excludes clerical):** 290 (2015-16), 300 (2017-18), 310 (2019-23), 300 (2024-25), 310 (2026). Investment staff rose from 150 to 170.

**Regulatory AUM (gross, includes leverage), at each year-end:**

| Year-end | $B |
|---|---|
| 2014 | 65.0 |
| 2015 | 71.8 |
| 2016 | 97.0 |
| 2017 | 130.8 |
| 2018 | 130.9 |
| 2019 | 166.0 |
| 2020 | 130.9 |
| 2021 | 121.8 |
| 2022 | 106.0 |
| 2023 | 89.3 |
| 2024 | 92.0 |
| 2025 | 96.4 |

**Medallion net capital** (sum of feeder-fund asset values at year-end) was $12.5-15.6B at YE2014-2017, $11.7B/$11.0B at YE2018/2019, then $20.5B, $28.2B, $25.3B and $19.2B at YE2020-2023. The Medallion master fund held $61.2B of levered gross assets at YE2025.

**Medallion fees:** 5% management / 44% performance through 2020; management cut to 4% from 2021-01-01; performance 36-44% from 2022. Fee-free employee retirement interests were redeemed in 2022.

**Medallion returns:** Zuckerman's Appendix 1 (via Cornell's Table 1) gives:

| Year | Net | Gross | Fund size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2015 | 36.0% | 69.3% | $9.5B |
| 2016 | 35.6% | 68.6% | $9.5B |
| 2017 | 45.0% | 85.4% | $10B |
| 2018 | 40.0% | 76.4% | $10B |

2020 was +76% net (about 141% gross). Q1 2021 was +9.7%.

**Derived Medallion gross trading P&L:** about $7.6B (2015), $7.9B (2016), $10.1B (2017), $9.8B (2018) and about $15.5B (2020). Each carries about ±$1.5-2.5B, reflecting the range between Zuckerman's fund size and the ADV feeder figures.

**Outside funds (RIEF/RIDA/RIDGE):**
- Master-fund gross assets peaked at $114B at YE2019 and fell to $26B at YE2025. Net-AUM anchors: RIEF about $36B, RIDA $15B and RIDGE $14.3B at the start of 2020; RIEF under $20B and RIDA $3.6B in Nov-2024. RIDGE merged into RIDA on 2023-12-31.
- Returns found: RIEF -19.4% and RIDA -31.6% in 2020; RIEF +20.5% in 2021; RIEF +22.7% and RIDA +15.6% in 2024; through Oct-2025 RIEF -7.5% and RIDA -10.3%.
- Derived gross P&L: about -$14B in 2020 (so the firm total was roughly break-even), about +$4.9B in 2021 (RIEF only), about +$4.8B in 2024, and about -$1.6B through Oct-2025.

**Main gaps:** Medallion returns for 2019 and 2021-2026, and outside-fund returns for 2015-2019, 2022-2023 and 2026. The web-search quota ran out before these could be found.
